own_solution.law: Kirchhoff's voltage law gives R C dV_C/dt + V_C = E. With V_C(0)=0, V_C(t)=E[1-exp(-t/(R C))]. Here R C=0.100 s, so V_C(0.080 s)=12[1-exp(-0.8)]=6.60805243 V.
assumptions: The battery maintains an ideal constant emf with negligible internal resistance.
The resistor and capacitor are ideal, with negligible capacitor leakage and negligible wire resistance.
Each added circuit component is present when charging begins.

TC3C7.regime: The switch opens after the observation time of 80 ms; the stated 500 ms satisfies this condition.

T821E.regime: Battery disconnection occurs after the observation time of 80 ms; the stated 500 ms satisfies this condition.

notes: Both added series-resistor sentences give total resistance 7 kΩ and time constant 0.140 s, yielding 12[1-exp(-0.080/0.140)] V. The tray and drawer resistors have no electrical connection to the charging circuit. All resistor variants consistently specify 2 kΩ. Both interruption variants consistently specify 500 ms and describe events occurring after the requested measurement. The ideal-component assumptions are conventional for this elementary RC problem.
